regime.method: 8 simple checks look at groups of markets over the last week and the last month. Each check votes risk-on (investors look comfortable owning riskier things), risk-off (investors look defensive) or neutral. The banner says risk-on or risk-off only when at least 60% of the checks that have data lean the same way and no more than 1 leans the other way; otherwise it says mixed.
regime.notice: A plain checklist of market groups, for research. It describes how markets behaved over the last week and month. It does not predict what comes next and it is not investment advice. No model chooses this label.

executive_summary.headline: Global money flows show monthly risk-off conditions easing into a mixed weekly picture, as participation improves across fixed income, equity sectors, and real estate while metals face recent outflows.
executive_summary.rotation_view: Across the month, broader money flows remain outflow-led with a risk-off tone, led by pressure in country markets, small-cap equities, metals, and crypto. However, short-term trends show improvement as weekly participation turns mixed. Weekly inflows shifted toward equity sectors, small-cap equities, real estate, and bonds, including long Treasury proxies and investment-grade credit. Conversely, metals experienced weekly pressure with outflows from gold, silver, and copper. Daily momentum remains mixed, though crypto logged recent daily volume-backed exits.
executive_summary.drivers_view: In corporate headlines, Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, JPMorgan, and Nvidia remain in focus amid discussions regarding artificial intelligence, computing capacity, and regulatory export considerations. On the macroeconomic front, Federal Reserve total assets, Treasury General Account balances, and central bank balance sheets for the European Central Bank and Bank of Japan show contraction, alongside rising US Treasury benchmark daily par yields.
